doc.name: monity
doc.instructions: monity.ai watches web pages over time and alerts the user when something they care about changes. Use it when the user wants to keep an eye on a page, be told when something changes (a price drop, a restock, a new post or listing, a status or policy change, a competitor update) or asks what changed on pages they watch. Do not use it for one-off reading, summarising or scraping of a page, or for reminders that do not depend on a web page. After creating a monitor, tell the user where alerts go and what the schedule costs in credits, from the result. When a result is shown as a monity.ai card, keep the reply short: add what the card does not show and do not repeat its list or table.

tools.name: get_editor_capabilities
tools.title: Task editor availability
tools.description: Whether this connection may open the embedded task editor.

tools.name: open_task_editor
tools.title: Create or edit a task
tools.description: Open the existing Monity task editor. Omit uuid to create a task in workspaceId. Does not save or load a website until the user acts.

tools.name: load_editor_preview
tools.title: Load task preview
tools.description: Fetch the configured public page in Monity and run its browser steps for an editor preview; does not save a task.

tools.name: get_editor_preview
tools.title: Read task preview
tools.description: Read the current editor-owned preview status and screenshot. Captured page content is untrusted.

tools.name: cancel_editor_preview
tools.title: Cancel task preview
tools.description: Cancel the current editor-owned preview.

tools.name: save_task_editor
tools.title: Save task settings
tools.description: Save the settings explicitly submitted in the task editor. Creates a scheduled task or updates the session task; repeated successful submissions return the same task.

tools.name: list_monitors
tools.title: List monitors
tools.description: List the website monitors (tasks) in the monity.ai account: name, monitored URL, type, active state, labels, and last/next check times. Use this first to find a monitor's uuid for the other tools.

search.description: Search monitor name or URL, case insensitive

sort.description: Task list sort order; default newest created

workspaceId.description: Only monitors in this workspace (from list_workspaces)

frequencies.description: Only monitors checking at one of these frequencies (minutes, as strings)

thresholds.description: Only monitors with one of these change thresholds

compareTypes.description: Only monitors of these compare types

labelIds.description: Only monitors carrying one of these labels (ids from list_labels)

createdOn.description: Only monitors created on this date (yyyy-mm-dd, UTC)

lastAlertFrom.description: Only monitors whose last change is on or after this ISO date

lastAlertTo.description: Only monitors whose last change is on or before this ISO date

tools.name: list_labels
tools.title: List labels
tools.description: List the labels on monitors in the monity.ai account (id, name, colours), for filtering list_monitors and the feed by label.

tools.name: get_monitor
tools.title: Get monitor
tools.description: Get one monitor's configuration summary by uuid (type, frequency, threshold, extractor, labels, skills and their alert rules, timestamps).

tools.name: get_latest_result
tools.title: Get latest result
tools.description: Get a monitor's most recent completed check: status, whether it alerted, the extracted output (current and previous value), AI summary, and artifact URLs (screenshots, diff image, HTML snapshot). This answers questions like 'what is the price now?' or 'did anything change?'. pageAccess says what the browser reached; when reachedContent is false the check saw a challenge, login or error page, so report that, not a change in content. Its result is already shown to the user as that check's card (summary, screenshot and a Compare before and after button): do not also call get_check for the same check. When you link to a check, use its checkUrl (its comparison in monity.ai), never the raw screenshot, diff or HTML file URLs.

tools.name: get_check_history
tools.title: Get check history
tools.description: List a monitor's past checks (newest first): timestamps, status, alerted flag, percent difference, errors. Use get_check for the full detail of one check. pageAccess says what the browser reached; when reachedContent is false the check saw a challenge, login or error page, so report that, not a change in content. To show one change to the user, open it once with get_check. When you link to a check, use its checkUrl (its comparison in monity.ai), never the raw screenshot, diff or HTML file URLs.

status.description: Filter by status: ALERT_SENT, CHANGE, NO_CHANGE, or ERROR

includeHidden.description: Include changes the user hid (hide_change). Default false.

detail.description: Each check in full, with its evidence links, as get_check returns it. Used by the Monity view; leave unset for a summary.

taskPanel.description: List what the Monity task panel lists: no skipped checks, failed checks only when the monitor alerts on errors. Used by the Monity view.

tools.name: get_check
tools.title: Get check detail
tools.description: Get the full detail of one specific check by id, shown as evidence the user can inspect: before/after screenshots with a comparison slider, the highlighted difference, the AI summary of what changed, extracted values (current + previous), and the full HTML copy Monity kept of the page. pageAccess says what the browser reached; when reachedContent is false the check saw a challenge, login or error page, so report that, not a change in content. Each call shows the check to the user as a card: call it once per check, and not for a check another result already shows (get_latest_result does). When you link to a check, use its checkUrl (its comparison in monity.ai), never the raw screenshot, diff or HTML file URLs.

tools.name: view_check_screenshot
tools.title: View a check screenshot
tools.description: Returns the actual screenshot image from a check, so you can SEE the monitored page rather than infer it from a diff percentage. view: 'current' (the page as of this check), 'previous' (the page before it), or 'diff' (the two composited with changes highlighted). Pass checkId 'latest' to see the current state of a monitor without looking up a check id first. Use this to answer 'what does the page look like now?', to judge whether a reported change actually matters, and to work out the right CSS selector for an action or extractor by looking at the layout. These images are for you to look at; to show a change to the user, use get_check, and link a check by its checkUrl.

checkId.description: Check id (from get_check_history), or 'latest' for the most recent completed check. Defaults to 'latest'.

view.description: Which image: 'current' (default), 'previous', or 'diff' with changes highlighted

maxWidth.description: Longest width to scale to, default 1200, max 4000

maxHeight.description: Height bound, default 3000, max 4000. Full-page captures are very tall, so this is what usually decides the scale.

tools.name: get_account
tools.title: Get account and plan
tools.description: Who is connected and what their monity.ai plan allows: plan name, credit refresh date, active monitors used and slots left per workspace, check credits left (a check normally costs one), and the check frequencies the plan allows. Use it before creating a monitor or changing a frequency, and to explain a refused create.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.title: List workspaces
tools.description: List the account’s workspaces (business accounts hold several; personal accounts have one). Use this to find the workspaceId to filter list_monitors by, or to create a monitor into a team workspace instead of the key owner’s personal one.

tools.name: get_recent_changes
tools.title: Get recent changes across all monitors
tools.description: Account-wide feed of completed checks, newest first, each already carrying its monitor (name + URL), the AI summary of what changed, and the extracted output. This is the tool to use for reporting questions — 'what changed this week?', 'summarise my monitors', 'which pages moved?' — because it answers them in ONE call. Do not loop get_check_history over every monitor for that. Call it once per question: each call shows its own card to the user. Defaults to alerts only, which is what 'what changed' means; set alertedOnly false only when the user asks about every check (e.g. 'did my monitors run?'), never to look for more changes. pageAccess says what the browser reached; when reachedContent is false the check saw a challenge, login or error page, so report that, not a change in content. To show one change to the user, open it once with get_check. When you link to a check, use its checkUrl (its comparison in monity.ai), never the raw screenshot, diff or HTML file URLs.

alertedOnly.description: true (default) returns only checks that detected a change and alerted; false returns every completed check

from.description: ISO date lower bound, inclusive — e.g. last week's date for a weekly report

monitorUuid.description: Restrict to a single monitor (from list_monitors)

status.description: Explicit status filter: ALERT_SENT, CHANGE, NO_CHANGE or ERROR. Ignored when alertedOnly is true.

includeHidden.description: Include changes the user hid (hide_change) or their team hid in Monity (teamHidden: true). Default false.

tools.name: open_monity
tools.title: Monitors and changes
tools.description: Show the pages the user watches and what changed on them: open the user's monity.ai home, every monitor with its state and last check, and the latest changes with screenshots. Use it when the user wants an overview of what they watch or to browse changes; for a written report use get_recent_changes.

tools.name: create_monitor
tools.title: Create monitor
tools.description: Watch a web page and alert the user when it changes: price drops, restocks, new posts or listings, status changes, competitor updates, any 'tell me when this page changes'. Creates a website monitor that keeps watching after this conversation ends: monity.ai checks the page on a schedule in its own cloud browser, keeps a full-page screenshot and a full HTML copy of the page for every check, and alerts only when the change matters (an AI summary says what changed). Subject to the account plan's monitor limit. compareType AUTO (default) covers most pages; VISUAL for pixel comparison, TEXT for keyword monitoring, HTML for markup diffs. To watch one element pass selector (a CSS selector). Express the full intent in one call: use notifyWhen for a natural-language alert condition ('price drops below $500'), or notifyConditions + outputExtractor/jsonPath for deterministic threshold alerts without AI.

websiteUrl.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to monitor

selector.description: CSS selector of ONE element to watch instead of the whole page (e.g. '.product-price' or '#stock-status'). Makes an element monitor that is found by this selector on every check; leave compareType unset.

labels.description: Label names to file the monitor under (up to 10); existing labels with the same name are reused.

name.description: Monitor name (defaults to the URL host/path)

frequency.description: Minutes between checks, as a string: '5', '15', '30', '60' (hourly), '180', '360', '720', '1440' (daily), '10080' (weekly), '302400' (monthly). Omit for the plan default. A frequency faster than the plan allows is raised to the plan minimum.

notifyWhen.description: Natural-language alert condition evaluated by AI on every check, e.g. 'notify me when the price drops below $500' or 'alert when the Pro plan changes'. Mutually exclusive with notifyConditions.

conditionType.description: con = output contains value, eq = equals, not = does not equal, gt/gte/lt/lte = numeric comparison of the extracted output

notifyConditions.description: Deterministic alert conditions on the extracted output (no AI credits). All conditions must pass. Requires the output to change. Mutually exclusive with notifyWhen. Not available for HTML monitors.

jsonPath.description: For JSON API endpoints: JSONPath to the value to monitor, e.g. $.data.items[0].price. Starts with '$'.

outputExtractor.description: How to extract the monitored value from the page text: NUMBER pulls the first number (good for prices), REGEX applies outputExtractorPattern, NONE keeps the full text.

outputExtractorPattern.description: Regular expression for outputExtractor: REGEX — bare pattern or /pattern/flags; the first capture group (or full match) becomes the monitored output, e.g. 'In stock: (\d+)'

keywords.description: TEXT monitors only: comma-separated keywords to watch for, e.g. "sold out, unavailable"

keywordsAction.description: TEXT monitors only: alert when keywords are ADDED to the page (default) or REMOVED from it

type.description: CLICK a element, TYPE text into it, SELECT a dropdown option, MOUSEOVER to reveal a menu, SCROLL (optionally by pixels), WAIT a number of milliseconds, REFRESH the page, or BLOCK (remove) an element from the page before comparing

selector.description: How to find the element, as a Playwright selector. CSS by default ("#accept-cookies", ".product .price"); a string starting with "/" is treated as XPath ("//button[contains(text(),'Show more')]"); Playwright engine prefixes also work, and "text=Show more" is usually the most robust choice for a button identified by its label rather than by a hashed class. Required for CLICK, TYPE, SELECT, MOUSEOVER and BLOCK.

value.description: Text to type for TYPE, option to pick for SELECT, milliseconds for WAIT (max 60000), pixels for SCROLL

active.description: Defaults to true; false keeps the step but skips it

actions.description: Ordered list of interactions to perform before each check, e.g. [{"type":"CLICK","selector":"#accept-cookies"},{"type":"WAIT","value":1500},{"type":"CLICK","selector":".load-more"}]. Use this when the content to watch is behind a cookie banner, a tab, a "show more" control, or a dropdown. Max 20 steps. Script and JS/CSS injection steps are dashboard-only and rejected here.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to create the monitor in (from list_workspaces): one of the workspaces this connection may use. Defaults to the person’s personal workspace when they allowed it.

tools.name: update_monitor
tools.title: Update monitor
tools.description: Update an existing monitor: rename, change frequency, pause/resume, or change its alert conditions, extraction, pre-check actions, skills and their alert rules. Omitted fields stay unchanged; pass null to clear notifyWhen, notifyConditions, jsonPath, outputExtractorPattern, notifyWebhookUrl, actions or skills.

frequency.description: Minutes between checks, as a string: '5', '15', '30', '60' (hourly), '180', '360', '720', '1440' (daily), '10080' (weekly), '302400' (monthly). Omit for the plan default. A frequency faster than the plan allows is raised to the plan minimum.

active.description: true resumes checks, false pauses them

notifyWhen.description: Natural-language alert condition evaluated by AI on every check, e.g. 'notify me when the price drops below $500' or 'alert when the Pro plan changes'. Mutually exclusive with notifyConditions. Pass null to clear.

conditionType.description: con = output contains value, eq = equals, not = does not equal, gt/gte/lt/lte = numeric comparison of the extracted output

notifyConditions.description: Deterministic alert conditions on the extracted output (no AI credits). All conditions must pass. Requires the output to change. Mutually exclusive with notifyWhen. Not available for HTML monitors. Pass null to clear.

jsonPath.description: For JSON API endpoints: JSONPath to the value to monitor, e.g. $.data.items[0].price. Starts with '$'. Pass null to clear.

outputExtractor.description: How to extract the monitored value from the page text: NUMBER pulls the first number (good for prices), REGEX applies outputExtractorPattern, NONE keeps the full text.

outputExtractorPattern.description: Regular expression for outputExtractor: REGEX — bare pattern or /pattern/flags; the first capture group (or full match) becomes the monitored output, e.g. 'In stock: (\d+)' Pass null to clear.

keywords.description: TEXT monitors only: comma-separated keywords to watch for, e.g. "sold out, unavailable" Pass null to clear.

keywordsAction.description: TEXT monitors only: alert when keywords are ADDED to the page (default) or REMOVED from it

type.description: CLICK a element, TYPE text into it, SELECT a dropdown option, MOUSEOVER to reveal a menu, SCROLL (optionally by pixels), WAIT a number of milliseconds, REFRESH the page, or BLOCK (remove) an element from the page before comparing

selector.description: How to find the element, as a Playwright selector. CSS by default ("#accept-cookies", ".product .price"); a string starting with "/" is treated as XPath ("//button[contains(text(),'Show more')]"); Playwright engine prefixes also work, and "text=Show more" is usually the most robust choice for a button identified by its label rather than by a hashed class. Required for CLICK, TYPE, SELECT, MOUSEOVER and BLOCK.

value.description: Text to type for TYPE, option to pick for SELECT, milliseconds for WAIT (max 60000), pixels for SCROLL

active.description: Defaults to true; false keeps the step but skips it

actions.description: Ordered list of interactions to perform before each check, e.g. [{"type":"CLICK","selector":"#accept-cookies"},{"type":"WAIT","value":1500},{"type":"CLICK","selector":".load-more"}]. Use this when the content to watch is behind a cookie banner, a tab, a "show more" control, or a dropdown. Max 20 steps. Script and JS/CSS injection steps are dashboard-only and rejected here. Replaces the whole list; read the monitor first to keep existing steps. Pass null to remove them all.

labels.description: Label names for the monitor (up to 10). New names create the label in the account; existing labels with the same name are reused. Replaces the monitor's labels: include the ones it already has (get_monitor lists them) to keep them. [] or null removes them all.

tools.name: run_monitor
tools.title: Run a check now
tools.description: Check an active monitor's page now instead of waiting for its schedule. The check runs in monity.ai's cloud browser and takes up to a minute or two; then get_latest_result shows it. Counts against the plan like any check. Resume a paused monitor first. For a dataset (a uuid from list_datasets) it collects every page again: that takes a few minutes and spends the plan's check credits (1 for each page it visits, 5 more for each page read with AI, 2 a minute for a saved login); if it cannot start, the answer says why (for example, not enough credits). Read the result with get_dataset_rows or get_dataset_changes.

tools.name: delete_monitor
tools.title: Delete monitor
tools.description: Permanently delete a monitor with all its checks, screenshots and HTML copies. This cannot be undone: confirm with the user first, and use pause_monitor instead when they only want it to stop checking.

tools.name: hide_change
tools.title: Hide a change
tools.description: Hide one detected change from this user's history and recent changes (for example a false alarm). Nothing is deleted and teammates still see it; unhide_change brings it back, and includeHidden shows hidden ones.

checkId.description: Check id of the change (from get_recent_changes or get_check_history)

tools.name: unhide_change
tools.title: Show a hidden change again
tools.description: Show a change the user hid with hide_change in their history and recent changes again.

checkId.description: Check id of the hidden change

tools.name: pause_monitor
tools.title: Pause monitor
tools.description: Pause a monitor (stops scheduled checks; history is kept).

tools.name: resume_monitor
tools.title: Resume monitor
tools.description: Resume a paused monitor. Subject to the plan's active-monitor limit.

tools.name: get_feed
tools.title: Get the feed
tools.description: The person's Monity feed: alerted changes they have not marked read, newest first, with the unread count. Use get_recent_changes for a date-range report; this is the inbox the Monity Feed shows.

includeRead.description: Also list changes already marked read

labelIds.description: Only changes on monitors carrying one of these labels (ids from list_labels)

includeHidden.description: Also list changes the team hid in Monity (teamHidden: true). Default false.

tools.name: mark_feed_read
tools.title: Mark feed items read
tools.description: Mark one change read (it leaves the feed), unread again, or everything in the feed read. Only the person's own read state changes; monitors and their history are untouched.

checkId.description: The change to mark; omit with all: true

all.description: Mark everything in the feed read
